x.hook: Institutional LPs will not deploy capital into pooled credit.
x.copy:
Pooled lending contains a structural defect that risk desks cannot accept. When a health factor fails in a shared pool, the insolvency is socialized. Every passive depositor absorbs the bad debt of the worst borrower.

Health factor calculations in pooled architectures evaluate an individual position, but enforce risk against a shared balance sheet. If a large liquidation stalls during market stress, the pool eats the deficit. The liquidity you supplied to earn low-risk yield becomes collateral for someone else's default.

SmartAccount sandboxes solve this at the execution layer. On Soroban, Vanna isolates capital into discrete contract instances rather than commingling deposits into a single vulnerability surface. Risk parameters run locally: a 1.10x Health Factor floor is enforced with ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, catching liquidations before bad debt can generate. If a position fails, the failure is quarantined to that specific SmartAccount.

Passive liquidity stays protected because it was never co-mingled with toxic leverage. 

Walkthrough video attached breaking down the contract execution flow.

Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

linkedin.hook: Why pooled lending models fail institutional insolvency standards.
linkedin.copy:
Most DeFi lending protocols operate on a commingled balance sheet. While this design bootstrapped early decentralized finance, it creates an irreconcilable property rights conflict for institutional liquidity providers. In a shared pool, health factor calculations monitor borrower solvency, but the liquidation shortfall is socialized across every depositor. If an illiquid position degrades faster than liquidators can clear it, passive capital takes an unhedged haircut for risk it never priced.

From an institutional perspective, this commingling turns low-risk yield provision into systemic underwriting. Vanna addresses this by separating credit execution from shared pool liquidity on Stellar Soroban. Instead of dumping assets into a monolithic pool contract, each borrower interacts through an isolated SmartAccount sandbox. Risk is tracked at the sandbox perimeter, maintaining a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. Powered by ~320ms Mercury indexer latency, the system evaluates and resolves margin degradation before positions cross into structural insolvency.

By isolating account state, bad debt cannot cascade into passive liquidity reserves. Institutional participants get deterministic containment: you only underwrite the risks you explicitly select, with zero exposure to third-party pool failures. We have deployed this architecture to testnet for institutional review. Deploy your testnet SmartAccount sandbox at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Why pooled lending health factors fail institutional risk models (and how isolated SmartAccounts fix this on Soroban)
reddit.copy:
The standard approach to DeFi lending has a major blind spot: the relationship between health factor calculations and insolvency contagion.

In protocols based on pooled liquidity, you deposit into a common vault, receive a receipt token, and borrowers draw against that shared reserve. The health factor measures how close an individual borrower is to liquidation. The problem appears when market depth drops or oracle updates lag. If a position drops below a 1.0x health factor before a liquidator steps in, the resulting bad debt does not stay with the borrower. It gets written off against the entire pool.

Passive LPs who simply wanted stable yield find their principal socialized to cover toxic debt from exotic collateral. For institutions, this creates unacceptable legal and balance-sheet risk.

Vanna takes a different architectural route on Stellar Soroban by moving to isolated SmartAccount sandboxes.

Instead of a monolithic vault holding all user funds, borrowing and leverage occur inside dedicated SmartAccount contracts. Health factor calculations are bound strictly to that sandbox environment. We set a 1.10x Health Factor floor, which is constantly fed by ~320ms Mercury indexer latency to monitor collateral health in near real-time. Because transaction costs on Soroban remain predictable at 0.00014 XLM fixed gas, liquidation transactions are not priced out by network congestion during volatility.

Most importantly, if an extreme black swan event renders an account insolvent, the loss is contained entirely within that SmartAccount. It cannot infect passive lenders or other independent positions.

We are currently testing these isolated sandboxes on Soroban testnet and want technical feedback on the contract boundaries and health factor mechanics.

Testnet deployment interface: test.stellar.vanna.finance

Disclosure: I am a core contributor at Vanna Protocol building credit infrastructure on Stellar Soroban.
